_comment: THE USER'S SEED-6 T4 BOARD (2026-09-10), and unlike seed 9 this one SATISFIES their rule
outright -- the failure was in EXECUTION, not in the trigger.
Kitchen (+Overgrowth +Trace of Abundance) = 4, Brushland (+Fertile Ground +Wild Growth) = 3,
Adarkar Wastes = 1: eight mana a tap. Peregrine Drake untaps up to FIVE, so every blink
recovers all three lands, and Eldrazi Displacer's {2}{C} is {C} under Training Grounds -- net
+7 a pass, with two colourless sources (Adarkar, Brushland) against one {C} pip. Kitchen's
'{4},{T}: Investigate' plus the Clue's own {2} is the draw engine the user had already been
hand-looping for five cards before they clicked.
What they got: thirteen draws, thirteen blinks, and 'the loop ran; the kill did not land' --
with a 60-iteration request and ~30 cards still in the library. See Session 15d for the two
causes; this fixture is the frame, and it must be OFFERED and VERIFIED.
_library_comment: WHAT THIS FIXTURE PINS. The Living Wish is THIRTEEN CARDS DOWN -- where the user's actually
was -- so the loop has to dig the whole way to it and then still run the finish CHAIN on their
real board: bank -> Kitchen investigate -> crack the Clue -> draw -> (x13) -> cast Living Wish
-> fetch Dimensional Infiltrator (blue, since the board makes no black) -> deploy it inside the
loop -> exile fifty cards. It runs the full sixty iterations, pays 26 draws, and wins.
IT USED TO PIN ONLY THE SHALLOW CASE (wish on top, one draw, x31), because the deep dig did
not work: the loop reached ten draws and stopped. Session 15d found and fixed two causes and
recorded a third as open. That third one is fixed now -- MTG_COMBO_OFF_DRAW_TRIAL -- so the
fixture is set to the depth the user actually had, which strictly subsumes the shallow chain.
THE BISECTION THAT LOCATED IT, kept because the shape of the evidence is the lesson. Walking
the wish's depth gave a cliff between 4 and 6 cards down and then IDENTICAL numbers at every
depth past it -- 6 blinks, 10 draws, no wish, every time. A dig that is genuinely too deep
degrades with depth; one that is constant is not about the dig at all. MTG_EDF_LOOP_TRACE:
k=6 enter             cost={C} float{c1} avail{g3 c1 *5}
k=6 post-draw-sink    cost={C} float{}   avail{}
STOP at k=6: pay-failed
Nine mana and a colourless went in, nothing came out, and the activation the guard was there
to protect costs ONE MANA. SpendSurplusOnDrawSinks' guard was a POOLED ManaPool::CanPay, which
cannot see that one land serves one of its modes (Brushland taps for {C} OR {G}/{W}) nor that
the sequential payment picks greedily -- so `{4}` was paid off the very sources the pending
`{C}` needed. It is now a REAL TRIAL on a copy of the state, the same repair
MTG_COMBO_OFF_SINK_TRIAL made for the damage sink.
AFTER, by wish depth (1, 2, 4 were already green; 6 and deeper were not):
depth  1 -> 31 blinks, WIN      depth  9 -> 60 blinks, WIN
depth  2 -> 37 blinks, WIN      depth 11 -> 60 blinks, WIN
depth  4 -> 49 blinks, WIN      depth 12 -> 60 blinks, WIN
depth  6 -> 60 blinks, WIN      depth 13 -> 60 blinks, 26 draws, WIN   <- this fixture
`[finish] guard-refused=12` on this board is the trial doing its job: it declines the draws
that would starve the loop and pays the 26 that would not.
